passages.text: A Psalm of Asaph.
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this psalm.
Asaph was a leader among the Levites.
He served as a musician in the temple.
This psalm is his song or prayer.

passages.text: Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart.
passages.sermon: This is a psalm of Asaph.\r\nGod is good to Israel.\r\nGod is good to people who are pure in heart.
passages.original: מִזְמ֗וֹר לְאָ֫סָ֥ף אַ֤ךְ ט֭וֹב לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אֱלֹהִ֗ים לְבָרֵ֥י לֵבָֽב׃

passages.text: But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled; my steps had nearly slipped.
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this psalm.
Asaph speaks about himself.
My feet almost stumbled.
My steps nearly slipped.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֗י כִּ֭מְעַט נָטוּי רַגְלָ֑י כְּ֝אַ֗יִן שֻׁפְּכָה אֲשֻׁרָֽי׃

passages.text: For I envied the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
passages.sermon:
I saw wicked people living in prosperity.
I saw arrogant people enjoying peace.
I envied these arrogant people.
I envied the prosperity of the wicked.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ קִ֭נֵּאתִי בַּֽהוֹלְלִ֑ים שְׁל֖וֹם רְשָׁעִ֣ים אֶרְאֶֽה׃

passages.text: They have no struggle in their death; their bodies are well-fed.
passages.sermon: The wicked do not struggle when they die.\r\nTheir bodies are healthy and strong.
passages.original: כִּ֤י אֵ֖ין חַרְצֻבּ֥וֹת לְמוֹתָ֗ם וּבָרִ֥יא אוּלָֽם׃

passages.text: They are free of the burdens others carry; they are not afflicted like other men.
passages.sermon:
The wicked are the subject here.
The wicked do not suffer the troubles that other people face.
The wicked do not experience the burdens that ordinary people endure.
The wicked are not afflicted like other men.
passages.original: בַּעֲמַ֣ל אֱנ֣וֹשׁ אֵינֵ֑מוֹ וְעִם־ אָ֝דָ֗ם לֹ֣א יְנֻגָּֽעוּ׃

passages.text: Therefore pride is their necklace; a garment of violence covers them.
passages.sermon:
These people are proud.
Pride surrounds their necks like a necklace.
Violence covers them like clothing.
passages.original: לָ֭כֵן עֲנָקַ֣תְמוֹ גַאֲוָ֑ה יַעֲטָף־ שִׁ֝֗ית חָמָ֥ס לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: From their prosperity proceeds iniquity; the imaginations of their hearts run wild.
passages.sermon:
These people live in prosperity.
Their prosperity leads them to do wrong.
Their hearts imagine many evil things.
Their thoughts have no limits.
passages.original: יָ֭צָא מֵחֵ֣לֶב עֵינֵ֑מוֹ עָ֝בְר֗וּ מַשְׂכִּיּ֥וֹת לֵבָֽב׃

passages.text: They mock and speak with malice; with arrogance they threaten oppression.
passages.sermon:
The wicked mock others.
They speak with malice.
They threaten to oppress people.
They speak with arrogance.
passages.original: יָמִ֤יקוּ׀ וִידַבְּר֣וּ בְרָ֣ע עֹ֑שֶׁק מִמָּר֥וֹם יְדַבֵּֽרוּ׃

passages.text: They set their mouths against the heavens, and their tongues strut across the earth.
passages.sermon:
The wicked speak boldly against God.
They use their mouths to challenge heaven.
They show pride in their words.
Their tongues move arrogantly across the earth.
They speak as if nothing can stop them.
They act as if they answer to no one.
passages.original: שַׁתּ֣וּ בַשָּׁמַ֣יִם פִּיהֶ֑ם וּ֝לְשׁוֹנָ֗ם תִּֽהֲלַ֥ךְ בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: So their people return to this place and drink up waters in abundance.
passages.sermon:
The wicked have people who follow them.
These people return to the wicked.
They come back to the place of the wicked.
They drink much water there.
They take in abundance from what is offered.
passages.original: לָכֵ֤ן׀ יָשִׁיב עַמּ֣וֹ הֲלֹ֑ם וּמֵ֥י מָ֝לֵ֗א יִמָּ֥צוּ לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: The wicked say, “How can God know? Does the Most High have knowledge?”
passages.sermon:
The wicked speak.
They ask, “How can God know?”
They question God’s knowledge.
They say, “Does the Most High understand?”
passages.original: וְֽאָמְר֗וּ אֵיכָ֥ה יָדַֽע־ אֵ֑ל וְיֵ֖שׁ דֵּעָ֣ה בְעֶלְיֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Behold, these are the wicked— always carefree as they increase their wealth.
passages.sermon:
The wicked live without worry.
They feel safe and secure.
They always seem at ease.
They keep gaining more wealth.
They become richer as time goes on.
passages.original: הִנֵּה־ אֵ֥לֶּה רְשָׁעִ֑ים וְשַׁלְוֵ֥י ע֝וֹלָ֗ם הִשְׂגּוּ־ חָֽיִל׃

passages.text: Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure; in innocence I have washed my hands.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a righteous person.
\r\nThe righteous person has kept his heart pure.
\r\nHe has done this with great effort.
\r\nHe has also washed his hands in innocence.
\r\nHe now believes this effort was in vain.
passages.original: אַךְ־ רִ֭יק זִכִּ֣יתִי לְבָבִ֑י וָאֶרְחַ֖ץ בְּנִקָּי֣וֹן כַּפָּֽי׃

passages.text: For I am afflicted all day long and punished every morning.
passages.sermon: I am afflicted all day long.\r\nI am punished every morning.
passages.original: וָאֱהִ֣י נָ֭גוּעַ כָּל־ הַיּ֑וֹם וְ֝תוֹכַחְתִּ֗י לַבְּקָרִֽים׃

passages.text: If I had said, “I will speak this way,” then I would have betrayed Your children.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a believer in God.
The speaker considers speaking in a certain way.
If the speaker had spoken in that way, the speaker would have betrayed God's children.
God's children are the faithful people who belong to God.
Betraying God's children means harming or misleading them.
The speaker chooses not to speak in that harmful way.
passages.original: אִם־ אָ֭מַרְתִּי אֲסַפְּרָ֥ה כְמ֑וֹ הִנֵּ֤ה ד֭וֹר בָּנֶ֣יךָ בָגָֽדְתִּי׃

passages.text: When I tried to understand all this, it was troublesome in my sight until I entered God’s sanctuary; then I discerned their end.
passages.sermon:
I tried to understand all this.
I found it very hard.
It troubled me.
I could not make sense of it.
Then I entered God’s sanctuary.
There, I understood their end.
passages.original: וָֽ֭אֲחַשְּׁבָה לָדַ֣עַת זֹ֑את עָמָ֖ל הִיא בְעֵינָֽי׃ עַד־ אָ֭בוֹא אֶל־ מִקְדְּשֵׁי־ אֵ֑ל אָ֝בִ֗ינָה לְאַחֲרִיתָֽם׃

passages.text: Surely You set them on slick ground; You cast them down into ruin.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power and authority.
God places the wicked on slippery ground.
God causes the wicked to fall.
God brings the wicked to destruction.
passages.original: אַ֣ךְ בַּ֭חֲלָקוֹת תָּשִׁ֣ית לָ֑מוֹ הִ֝פַּלְתָּ֗ם לְמַשּׁוּאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: How suddenly they are laid waste, completely swept away by terrors!
passages.sermon:
God destroys the wicked very quickly.
He brings them to ruin in a moment.
He sweeps them away all at once.
He removes them completely because of sudden terrors.
passages.original: אֵ֤יךְ הָי֣וּ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה כְרָ֑גַע סָ֥פוּ תַ֝֗מּוּ מִן־ בַּלָּהֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Like one waking from a dream, so You, O Lord, awaken and despise their form.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is the subject.
The Lord wakes up.
The Lord sees their form.
The Lord despises their form.
This happens like a person waking from a dream.
passages.original: כַּחֲל֥וֹם מֵהָקִ֑יץ אֲ֝דֹנָי בָּעִ֤יר׀ צַלְמָ֬ם תִּבְזֶֽה׃

passages.text: When my heart was grieved and I was pierced within, I was senseless and ignorant; I was a brute beast before You.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a human being who addresses God.
The speaker’s heart felt pain.
The speaker’s inner being felt wounded.
The speaker did not understand what was happening.
The speaker acted without wisdom.
The speaker was like a brute animal before God.
passages.original: כִּ֭י יִתְחַמֵּ֣ץ לְבָבִ֑י וְ֝כִלְיוֹתַ֗י אֶשְׁתּוֹנָֽן׃ וַאֲנִי־ בַ֭עַר וְלֹ֣א אֵדָ֑ע בְּ֝הֵמ֗וֹת הָיִ֥יתִי עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Yet I am always with You; You hold my right hand.
passages.sermon:
God, You are always with me.
You hold my right hand.
You do not leave me.
You guide and support me.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֣י תָמִ֣יד עִמָּ֑ךְ אָ֝חַ֗זְתָּ בְּיַד־ יְמִינִֽי׃

passages.text: You guide me with Your counsel, and later receive me in glory.
passages.sermon:
God gives me counsel.
God guides me with His wisdom.
After this life, God will receive me.
God will take me into glory.
passages.original: בַּעֲצָתְךָ֥ תַנְחֵ֑נִי וְ֝אַחַ֗ר כָּב֥וֹד תִּקָּחֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Whom have I in heaven but You? And on earth I desire no one besides You.
passages.sermon: The speaker addresses God.\r\nThe speaker says, "I have no one in heaven except You."\r\nThe speaker says, "On earth, I do not desire anyone besides You."
passages.original: מִי־ לִ֥י בַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְ֝עִמְּךָ֗ לֹא־ חָפַ֥צְתִּי בָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this psalm.
He trusted God.
My body may become weak.
My heart may fail.
God gives strength to my heart.
God is my portion forever.
passages.original: כָּלָ֥ה שְׁאֵרִ֗י וּלְבָ֫בִ֥י צוּר־ לְבָבִ֥י וְחֶלְקִ֗י אֱלֹהִ֥ים לְעוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: Those far from You will surely perish; You destroy all who are unfaithful to You.
passages.sermon:
God judges people.
God sees those who are far from Him.
People who are far from God will perish.
God destroys every person who is unfaithful to Him.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הִנֵּ֣ה רְחֵקֶ֣יךָ יֹאבֵ֑דוּ הִ֝צְמַ֗תָּה כָּל־ זוֹנֶ֥ה מִמֶּֽךָּ׃

passages.text: But as for me, it is good to draw near to God. I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may proclaim all Your works.
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this psalm.
Asaph was a worship leader in Israel.
He spoke about his relationship with God.
He said it is good for him to be near God.
He chose to make the Lord GOD his refuge.
He did this so he could tell about all of God's works.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֤י׀ קִֽרֲבַ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֗ים לִ֫י־ ט֥וֹב שַׁתִּ֤י׀ בַּאדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֣ה מַחְסִ֑י לְ֝סַפֵּ֗ר כָּל־ מַלְאֲכוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
